question: Johan walks 10 miles at an average rate of 2 miles per hour and returns on a bicycle at an average rate of 10 miles per hour. How long does the entire trip take him?
explanation: 🔖We know, \( v=\frac{s}{t}\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\therefore t=\frac{s}{v}\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\therefore Time to go=\frac{10}{2}=5 hour\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}and time to return=\frac{10}{1}=1 hour\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\therefore Total time=\left(5+1\right)=6 hour \)

question: In theis diagram AB=AC angle A = 40 degree and BD is perpendicular to AC at D. how many degrees are there in angle DBC?
explanation:
🔖\( △ABC এ AB=AC,\angle B=\angle C\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\therefore \angle A+\angle B+\angle C={180}^{\circ }\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\Rightarrow \angle B+\angle C={180}^{\circ }-{40}^{\circ }\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\Rightarrow \angle B+\angle C={140}^{\circ }\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\Rightarrow 2\angle B={140}^{\circ }\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\therefore \angle B={70}^{\circ }=\angle C\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}Again, △ABD এ \angle ADB={90}^{\circ }\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\angle A={40}^{\circ }\phantom{\rule{0ex}{0ex}}\therefore \angle DBA={180}^{\circ }-{90}^{\circ }-{40}^{\circ }={50}^{\circ } \)
\( \therefore \angle DBC=\angle ABC-\angle DBA={70}^{\circ }-{50}^{\circ }={20}^{\circ } \)
